title: Total random examples bound
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$. Put $\delta=1/(10|\mathcal F|)$, $\eta=\varepsilon/(2|\mathcal F|)$, and let $L$ be the least integer $k$ such that $2^k\geq\lceil 2/\delta\rceil$. If $N=\lceil 2L/\eta^2\rceil$ is the sample count per coefficient, then the total number $|\mathcal F|N$ of random examples satisfies $|\mathcal F|N\leq 16|\mathcal F|^3L/\varepsilon^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
